title: Space Tech Briefing — September 12, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space explorers! It's Friday, September 12th, 2026, and your daily dose of cosmic news is here, beaming straight into your ears! I'm thrilled to bring you the latest from the cutting edge of space technology.

First up, let's revisit a truly stellar achievement in our ongoing quest for new worlds! NASA recently unveiled the most comprehensive sky map ever compiled by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, or TESS. This incredible exoplanet hunter, launched back in 2018, has been meticulously scanning our universe for signs of planets orbiting distant stars. The new map is a breathtaking mosaic, a complete view of the starry sky, built from observations stretching from April 2018 all the way to September 2025. It stitches together 96 sectors of the sky, revealing nearly 6,000 vibrant objects – each one a confirmed or candidate exoplanet! What an astonishing testament to TESS's tireless work in charting new worlds!

And speaking of incredible journeys, let's turn our attention back to a familiar face in the astronaut corps. French astronaut Thomas Pesquet has officially begun his rigorous training for his next mission! Slated for 2027, Pesquet is set to take command of the Vast-PAM-1 mission, heading once again to the International Space Station. It's fantastic to see him gearing up for another command role, preparing to lead the charge aboard the orbiting laboratory. We'll be tracking his progress every step of the way!

That's all for your Space Technology Morning Briefing today, September 12th, 2026. Keep looking up, keep exploring, and have a fantastic day! We'll catch you back here tomorrow for more groundbreaking news from beyond our world.
